publications.title: Developing Robotic Process Automation (RPA) for Managing Electronic Book (E-book) in Digital Libraries
publications.abstract: Managing e-book collections in digital libraries requires high efficiency and accuracy to meet library needs. The implementation of Robotic Process Automation (RPA) with UiPath aims to automate manual processes in e-book management, including retrieving e-book descriptions, downloading covers, and uploading to library systems. This research aims to improve operational efficiency and quality of digital library services by developing RPA for e-book management in digital libraries. This research uses the waterfall model, which is a software development model with a systematic and sequential approach. The development stages are Identification, Analysis, Design, Development and Test, and Implementation. RPA E-book management with UiPath automates the download process of e-book covers, data collection of e-book bibliographic descriptions, and the process of managing and uploading e-books to the library system. The automation process succeeded in reducing manual errors in data input, thereby increasing the accuracy and consistency of e-book information. The research results indicate that the application of RPA in managing e-books in digital libraries is effective in increasing operational efficiency. Scenario-based workflow evaluations indicate that the automated system reduces processing duration from 15 minutes to 2 minutes per e-book. Under standard task-allocation modeling, this represents a 600% increase in output productivity (achieving 700% of the manual baseline output). This automation not only increases efficiency and data accuracy but also allows library staff to focus on other strategic tasks.

publications.title: HelioFITS Peek
publications.abstract: HelioFITS Peek teaches macOS Finder and Quick Look to read solar FITS files. A thumbnail extension renders each file in the colormap its header calls for, a Quick Look extension gives an interactive preview with pixel values, helioprojective coordinates, region statistics and multi-HDU blink comparison, and a Spotlight importer makes header fields searchable. A viewer app shows the full header, exports PNG and copies a sunpy snippet that loads the HDU on screen. It vendors CFITSIO (NASA HEASARC) under its own licence.

publications.title: Comparative Analysis of Social Media Discourse Structures on Appearance Management for Women with Disabilities: Focusing on Text Mining of Naver, Instagram, and YouTube
publications.abstract: This study examined platform-specific structures of social media discourse related to appearance management among women with disabilities across Naver, Instagram, and YouTube. Appearance management among women with disabilities extends beyond beautification to encompass multidimensional issues related to welfare, accessibility, and self-expression. Data were collected over a three-year period (January 2023–December 2025) using combinations of search terms related to women, disability, appearance management, and beauty. The data were analyzed using text mining, keyword analysis, word cloud visualization, semantic network analysis, and CONCOR clustering. After data refinement, 7,411 Naver documents, 1,240 Instagram posts, and text metadata from 302 YouTube videos were collected, and the integrated text metadata of 159 videos were included in the final analysis. Naver showed the highest network density (0.4474), with discourse primarily structured around policy, welfare, support, and education; Instagram (density = 0.3211) showed discourse centered on disability, barrier-free accessibility, welfare centers, beauty practices, and volunteering; and YouTube (density = 0.3000) showed discourse emphasizing disability types, education, welfare, healthcare, and beauty-related support. CONCOR analysis identified four discourse clusters on each platform, although their compositions differed substantially across platforms, with institution- and welfare-oriented clusters on Naver, practice- and accessibility-oriented clusters on Instagram, and a relatively broad education-and-beauty-support cluster on YouTube. Across the three platforms, disability- and beauty-related keywords occupied central positions in the semantic networks, whereas the surrounding keyword structures differed across platforms. The findings suggest that platform-specific content structures and communication affordances may be associated with differences in the organization of online discourse related to disability and beauty, providing empirical insights for the development of platform-specific beauty support programs and digital welfare strategies.

publications.title: Buying an AI MVP: Scope, Ownership and the Costs After Launch
publications.abstract: What does an AI MVP development quote actually buy? This Arcforth buyer report reviews eight public provider pages and turns their published terms into a practical brief for commissioning software. The review distinguishes discovery from implementation, payment-ready architecture from completed billing, and included support from continuing paid engineering. It examines scope, source-code ownership, account handover, AI acceptance and post-launch operating responsibilities. The five-page report includes a provider comparison, a reusable quote-request brief, a first-90-days budgeting framework and linked primary sources. An accompanying evidence package contains the observation ledger, collection metadata, review method and a Python script that reproduces the reported disclosure counts. Sources were observed on 29 October 2026. The purposive sample comprises five pricing-led discoveries and three consultative providers; one discovered MVP URL now redirects to an agent-services catalog. Findings describe information found on individual pages, not vendor quality or verified delivery performance. This is a public-offer review, not a representative market survey or product benchmark. Publisher: Arcforth, a product development provider with a commercial interest in the topic. Arcforth is discussed separately and excluded from comparative counts. AI tools assisted with organization and writing. See the report for methods, limitations and source links.

publications.title: Local Business Website Enquiry Checklist (India)
publications.abstract: An 18 point checklist that helps local businesses in India check whether their website helps customers find them and contact them. It covers Google Business Profile, Search Console, LocalBusiness structured data, page speed, tap to call, WhatsApp button, contact forms, maps, reviews and enquiry tracking. Prepared by ArcBig Solutions Pvt. Ltd., a web development and social media marketing agency in Modinagar, Delhi NCR, serving businesses since 2018. More at https://arcbig.com

publications.title: Distributionally robust chance-constrained standard quadratic optimization with Wasserstein ambiguity
publications.abstract: The standard quadratic optimization problem consists of minimizing a quadratic form over the standard simplex. It has highly relevant applications ranging from portfolio optimization to machine learning. However, if the quadratic form is neither convex nor concave, this problem is NP-hard. We study a distributionally robust chance-constrained variant whose ambiguity set is a Wasserstein ball around the sampled distribution and make four contributions. First, although the problem is nonconvex in the decision variable, we exploit its linear dependence on the uncertain matrix to reduce the problem to a mixed-integer quadratic optimization problem. Second, we show that a judicious choice of matrix norm---the entrywise maximum norm---makes this reformulation both exact and tractable, and we describe the induced worst-case distribution. Third, our formulation is, by construction, the minimization of the worst-case Value-at-Risk of the random quadratic form; this unifies it with existing frameworks for uncertain standard quadratic optimization problems, in particular under chance constraints, and we identify natural settings in which it collapses to a single deterministic instance. Finally, we report numerical experiments on positive-definite and indefinite instances which quantify how the model parameters drive the optimal value and solution time, and expose the computational cost of indefiniteness.

publications.title: Designing battery swapping and charging networks for electric freight transport under demand uncertainty
publications.abstract: Long-haul truck electrification requires rapid energy replenishment near freight demand, although dispersed hubs may lack sufficient grid capacity. We study a "Swap-Locally, Charge-Centrally" architecture embedded in a relay freight network: swapping remains close to freight flows, charging can be shifted to grid-suitable hubs, and co-location is retained where economical. A multi-period, two-stage stochastic location-inventory-fleet model coordinates station deployment, replenishment assignments and grid-bounded charging capacity with scenario-dependent battery stocks, batch sizes and incremental fleet requirements. Corridor electrification competes with temporary diesel operation. Building on submodularity-based constraint generation for location-inventory systems, we give an alternative scalar partial-minimization proof that the battery value function is submodular, show that the fleet recourse is affine in the binary swap-station decisions, and develop a Lovász-cut Benders decomposition with hub-period block cuts and a convex battery oracle with analytic gradients and memoization. On a seven-state southeastern U.S. freight network, the method reaches gaps below 0.01% on all five instances, the largest in about four minutes, whereas a strengthened extensive formulation reaches this tolerance only on the two smallest instances within three hours. Stochastic planning avoids the capacity shortfalls of a mean-value plan, and joint planning avoids the battery and fleet costs that sequential siting shifts downstream. The optimized network uses remote charging selectively, keeps most replenishment local, and expands geographic coverage before intensifying capacity within its committed deployment plan.

publications.title: Training language models in simulation for psychiatric intake
publications.abstract: In psychiatric practice, the clinical intake interview remains a primary diagnostic instrument, requiring the clinician to establish rapport while disentangling complex, overlapping presentations. Here, we show that multi-turn reinforcement learning (RL) in simulation environments improves language model performance on structured text-based psychiatric intake, spanning history-taking, differential diagnosis, and initial management planning. In a randomized, double-blind crossover study ($N = 60$ matched scenario pairs, 120 encounters) comparing the RL-trained agent against its identically prompted base model, 32 board-certified psychiatrists role-played standardized patients while a separate panel of 15 independent, board-certified psychiatrists scored the de-identified transcripts. The trained agent outperformed the base model in 76.7% of matched scenario pairs ($p < 0.0001$), with gains on an adapted clinical-examination rubric ($d_z = 0.77$, $p < 0.0001$), patient-centered communication (82.0% vs. 65.2%, $p < 0.001$), and differential diagnosis appropriateness (68.3% vs. 33.3%, $p < 0.001$). Across 127 psychiatrist-validated simulated intake scenarios, the trained agent nearly doubled its base model's clinical rubric score (0.706 vs. 0.379; composite reward 0.564 vs. 0.294, $p < 0.0001$). To systematically probe conversational safety, we established two Delphi-consensus taxonomies, of clinical safety risks and relational competencies, from which 256 challenging adversarial presentations were derived; we find that training in simulation environments more than halved under-triage of acute safety risks (12.9% vs. 30.5%, $p < 0.0001$). Simulation environments thus provide a controlled testbed for training and stress-testing psychiatric conversational agents, with gains that transferred to psychiatrist-enacted encounters, though residual gaps require safeguards and clinician oversight.

publications.title: EXPRESS: Revitalizing the Grocery Store Experience: An Empirical Study on the Spillover Effects of Experiential Services
publications.abstract:
Grocery retailers increasingly use experiential services to attract customers to their stores. However, it remains unclear whether these services generate positive
                    spillover
                    effects to core grocery sales or cannibalize existing demand. We provide the first empirical evidence by studying a grocery retailer that introduced a taphouse as its first experiential service and examining the underlying mechanisms.
                  
                  
                    We combine store transaction records with SafeGraph's point-of-interest data and survey data on product attributes. Using a quasi-experimental design, we specify a synthetic difference-in-differences estimator with staggered treatment timings. Our results show significant positive spillover effects. On average, stores that feature a taphouse experienced a 5.97% increase in daily sales volume, a 6.82% rise in sales revenue, a 5.76% increase in transactions, and a 6.18% expansion in product variety compared to stores without a taphouse. Our mechanism analyses suggest that these results are associated with activity through both
                    extensive
                    (newly observed customers) and
                    intensive
                    (greater purchasing activity among existing customers) margins. We find that an average order contains fewer but relatively higher-priced items, leaving average order value statistically unchanged. Newly acquired customers make relatively smaller purchases than existing customers, whose order size does not change significantly following the taphouse introduction. We also find that products complementary to the taphouse and those with a greater propensity for impulse purchasing account for larger shares of grocery sales following taphouse introduction. Finally, nearby competing supermarkets experience reductions in both total visits and unique visitors, suggesting that local competitive substitution may contribute to the observed customer expansion.
                  
                  To assess generalizability, we replicate the analysis with another grocery chain in a different region that introduced a full restaurant and obtain qualitatively similar results. Overall, the findings indicate that adding a taphouse can effectively increase grocery sales volume and revenue. Although high setup costs may deter adoption, our break-even analysis projects recovery in approximately 34 to 39 weeks from grocery-side gross-margin contributions alone, or 27 to 44 weeks when alternative assumptions about taphouse profitability, including operating losses, are incorporated.
